Are subarrays defined as contiguous segments of the original sequence, or can they be any subsequence (not necessarily contiguous)?
Is the array 1-indexed or 0-indexed for the purpose of describing positions, or does it not matter for the answer?
Must the subarray be non-empty but can it consist of a single element if that element appears elsewhere in the array?
Are there any constraints on the size of the integers beyond the given limits that could affect overflow or memory considerations?
Should the output be exactly “-1” (without quotes) when no such subarray exists, and no extra whitespace or newline characters?

inline_prompts: You are given a positive integer N and an integer sequence A = (A_1,A_2,\dots,A_N) of length N. Determine whether there exists a non-empty subarray of A that has a repeated value, occurring multiple times in A. If such a subarray exists, find the length of the shortest such subarray. Refer to the problem statement for specifications related to: Does the subarray need to contain at least two equal elements. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N A_1 A_2 \dots A_N Output If there is no subarray satisfying the condition in the problem statement, print -1. Otherwise, print the length of the shortest such subarray. Constraints - 1 \leq N \leq 2 \times 10^5 - 1 \leq A_i \leq 10^6 \ (1 \leq i \leq N) - All input values are integers.
